gen-dafont-blockletter-inter: Inter brings smooth, tube-like lines and counters that breathe, all in a tall lowercase. And Blockletter's squat, pencil-sketched display forms give it something blunt and precise to lean against.
gen-dafont-blockletter-mulish: Blockletter stands up top with a tall, squat-bellied display build, while Mulish below keeps its strokes uniform and its apertures wide. The sketchy heading gets room to speak.
gen-dafont-bloody-bitter: Bitter sets down slab-serif text with a very large lowercase and an s you can see straight through. Bloody saves its big round bowls for shouting; Bitter just holds steady.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-bespoke-sans: Sharp and refined, Bespoke Sans leaves generous space between its curve ends and stems. Under Bloody's big round bowls, it gives the heading's high lowercase a moderate, steadier partner.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-epunda-slab: Dignified and classic, Epunda Slab shows a visibly gaping c and tall rounded lowercase forms under Bloody's big round bowls. Both fonts favor roundness, and that shared softness is what ties them.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-fauna-one: Fauna One is a literary text serif with a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and descenders, and a generous entry into each e. Its strongest quality is how quietly it sits beneath Bloody's round bowls.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-glegoo: Glegoo reads refined and editorial, with big counters. Bloody is the one that commands attention with round bowls, while Glegoo's wide, unclosed curves do the patient work of carrying the text.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-kadwa: Kadwa is a classic serif with open-ended curves and a larger-than-usual x-height under Bloody's heavy display. Kadwa then keeps a long passage moving smoothly, with a scholarly, editorial feel.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-piazzolla: Big round bowls in lowercase give Bloody its commanding look, and Piazzolla's lowercase, nearly matching its capitals, has an e opened wide. Authority runs through both, one loud and one refined.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-pridi: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody its commanding presence. Pridi's small letters stand proud, almost capital-sized, so a modest text size would let it hold its own beneath the heading.
